metadata.source: Wildlife (Protection) Act, 1972 - Key Procedures and Processes

sanctuaryDeclaration.title: Declaration of Sanctuary (Sections 18-26A)
steps: State Government identifies area with ecological/faunal/floral significance
Issues notification declaring intention (Section 18)
Appoints Collector to determine rights (Section 18B)
Collector publishes proclamation (Section 21)
Inquiry into rights (Section 22)
Acquisition of rights (Section 24) - under RFCTLARR Act 2013 (2022)
Time limit for acquisition proceedings (Section 25A)
Final notification declaring sanctuary (Section 26A)
Chief Wild Life Warden assumes control (Section 33)
keyPoints: Cannot include reserve forest unless rights settled
2022: Management plans per Central Govt guidelines, Gram Sabha consultation in Scheduled Areas

nationalParkDeclaration.title: Declaration of National Park (Section 35)
steps: State Government identifies area with ecological significance
Issues notification declaring intention (Section 35(1))
2022: Sections 27-33A apply IMMEDIATELY on declaration of intent (Section 35(3A))
Rights determination process (similar to sanctuary)
2022: Alternative arrangements for affected persons till rights settled (Section 35(3B))
Final notification declaring National Park (Section 35(4))
Higher protection: no grazing, no habitat alteration

conservationReserveDeclaration.title: Declaration of Conservation Reserve (Sections 36A, 36B, 38(2A))
steps: State Government (or Central Government post-2022) identifies government-owned area
Consults local communities
Issues notification declaring conservation reserve
Constitutes Conservation Reserve Management Committee (Section 36B)
Committee: Forest Officer, Wildlife Warden, Panchayat rep, NGO rep, experts

communityReserveDeclaration.title: Declaration of Community Reserve (Sections 36C, 36D)
steps: Community/land owner agrees to protect wildlife on their land
State Government issues notification declaring community reserve
Constitutes Community Reserve Management Committee (Section 36D)
2022: Private land committee = owner + Forest Dept rep + Panchayat/tribal rep
Committee prepares management plan
keyPoints: 2022: Specific composition for private land reserves

tigerReserveNotification.title: Tiger Reserve Notification & Management (Sections 38V, 38W)
steps: State Government identifies area with tiger population
Prepares Tiger Conservation Plan (core + buffer)
Submits to NTCA for approval (Section 38V)
NTCA approves/modifies plan
State Government notifies tiger reserve
Core area = inviolate (critical tiger habitat)
Buffer area = co-existence zone
Voluntary relocation with consent & rehabilitation (Section 38V)
No boundary alteration without NTCA + National Board approval (Section 38W)
No de-notification without NTCA + National Board approval
keyPoints: Rights settlement under FRA 2006 before relocation

huntingPermit.title: Hunting Permit Procedure (Sections 11, 12)
steps: Application to Chief Wild Life Warden
Schedule I/II: ONLY if dangerous to human life/property OR disabled/diseased beyond recovery
Schedule III/IV: For education, research, scientific management
CWLW evaluates, may grant permit with conditions
Permit specifies: species, number, area, period, method
CANNOT be delegated (Section 5)
keyPoints: Schedule I/II: Extremely restricted (human safety/mercy only)

specifiedPlantPermit.title: Specified Plant Permit (Sections 17A, 17B)
steps: Prohibition on picking, uprooting, collecting specified plants (Schedule VI)
CWLW may grant permit for education, research, scientific management
Cultivation without licence prohibited (Section 17C)
Dealing without licence prohibited (Section 17D)
Stock declaration required (Section 17E)
Possession by licensee only (Section 17F)
Purchase from licensee only (Section 17G)
Plants become Government property (Section 17H)
keyPoints: Complete prohibition on Schedule VI plants

ownershipCertificate.title: Certificate of Ownership (Sections 40, 42, 42A)
steps: Declaration of possession within 30 days (Section 40)
Inquiry and inventory preparation (Section 41)
CWLW issues certificate of ownership (Section 42)
Certificate required for transfer/transport (Section 43)
2022: VOLUNTARY SURRENDER - give 7 days notice, surrender to CWLW, cert cancelled, NO compensation (Section 42A)
Surrendered items become State Government property

citESTradePermits.title: CITES Trade Permits (Chapter VB, Sections 49H-49L)
steps: Management Authority (ADG Forests+) issues permits
Scientific Authority advises on non-detriment findings
EXPORT (Section 49I): Appendix I/II - export permit; Appendix III - permit/certificate of origin
IMPORT (Section 49J): Appendix I - import permit + export permit/re-export cert; Appendix II - export permit/re-export cert; Appendix III - certificate of origin/export permit/re-export cert
RE-EXPORT (Section 49K): Appendix I/II - re-export certificate
INTRODUCTION FROM SEA (Section 49L): Appendix I/II - certificate of introduction from sea
All trade only at designated ports
Reporting to Management Authority mandatory
keyPoints: Appendix III: certificate of origin/export permit

possessionRegistrationCITES.title: Possession Registration for Schedule IV Species (Section 49M)
steps: Report possession of living Schedule IV animal to Management Authority
Authority may issue registration certificate if lawful possession
Report transfers (transferor AND transferee)
Report births of offspring
Report deaths
Breeding Appendix I species requires licence (Sections 49N-49O)
Central Govt may exempt species/quantities/periods
keyPoints: Mandatory reporting of possession, transfers, births, deaths
Breeding Appendix I = licence from CWLW

offenceInvestigation.title: Offence Investigation & Enforcement (Sections 50, 51, 55)
steps: Authorized officers: Director, CWLW, police, forest officers, customs, coast guard, Management Authority (2022), WCCB (2006)
Powers: entry, search, arrest without warrant, seizure (Section 50)
Seizure: animals, articles, trophies, scheduled specimens, vehicles, vessels
Sample collection for forensic analysis
Complaint to court by authorized officers only (Section 55)
Private person: 60-day notice to State Govt before complaint
Presumptions under Section 57 (burden on accused)
Compoundable offences: CWLW can compound up to ₹5 lakh (Section 54)
keyPoints: Arrest without warrant for cognizable offences

forfeitureProcedure.title: Forfeiture of Illegally Acquired Property (Chapter VIA, Sections 58A-58Y)
steps: Competent Authority identifies illegally acquired property
Show cause notice to person (Section 58E)
Seizure/freezing of property (Section 58F)
Administrator manages seized property (Section 58G)
Notice of forfeiture (Section 58H)
Forfeiture order if illegally acquired (Section 58I)
Burden of proof on ACCUSED (Section 58J)
Fine in lieu of forfeiture option (Section 58K)
Appeal to Appellate Tribunal within 45 days (Section 58O)
Bar of civil court jurisdiction (Section 58Q)

verminDeclaration.title: Vermin Declaration Procedure (Section 62)
steps: Central Government identifies Schedule II species causing damage
Issues notification declaring species as vermin for specific area/period
Declared species deemed NOT in Schedule II for that area/period
No penalty for hunting/killing declared vermin during notification period
2022: ONLY Schedule II species eligible (was Schedules III-V)

invasiveAlienSpeciesRegulation.title: Invasive Alien Species Regulation (Section 62A, 2022)
steps: Central Government identifies non-native species threatening wildlife/habitat
Issues notification regulating/prohibiting import, trade, possession, proliferation
Authorizes Director/officers to seize and dispose (including destruction)
Species not native to India, introduction/spread threatens wildlife/habitat
keyPoints: Addresses biodiversity threat from alien species
